exposure: N/A - This study developed a tool and defined indicators, but did not measure specific exposures in a patient cohort.
outcome: Use of the safe surgery checklist
Proportion of cases with complications graded >2 on the Clavien-Dindo scale
Time from emergency department presentation to non-elective abdominal surgery
Comparative income of patients compared with population
Proportion of patients facing catastrophic expenditure because of surgical care
cohort: N/A - This study focused on developing a tool and did not involve a patient cohort.
finding: The study successfully defined a novel, evidence-based tool consisting of 15 indicators across five dimensions (safety, effectiveness, patient-centeredness, timeliness, and equity) to measure the quality of surgical care in low-resource settings.
mod_finding: The developed tool includes 'rate of caesarean sections' as an indicator for effective surgical outcomes.
country: N/A - The study focuses on 'low-resource settings' globally.
